title: RFP-Admin Operations Guide — Run the Platform

lede: The complete operator’s manual: every screen in the admin console, in the order you use it — monitor sources, ingest and curate RFPs, push opportunities, release purchases, oversee every workflow and agent, and shadow-descend into any company to do the work.
Screenshots are the live console; every button, modal, and status value below is the real thing.
hero.badge: Complete surface · every screen, button, and status — verified against the live console

footer: govwin — RFP Pipeline Portal · RFP-Admin role. Canonical automation surface is /admin/workflows; /admin/process and /admin/processes are legacy lenses on the same runs. Companion guides: Customer-Admin, Collaborator.

sections.heading: Orientation — the admin console
sections.where: /admin  ·  sign in as an rfp_admin / master_admin
sections.lead: The admin console is where you run the platform: monitor sources, ingest and curate RFPs, release purchases, and oversee every automation and agent. This guide walks the whole surface, screen by screen, in the order you actually use it. Sign in with your RFP-admin credentials; the console opens on the Dashboard.

callouts.html: The seeded operator eric@rfppipeline.com is a master_admin — global access to every tenant plus the full admin surface. rfp_admin has the same console; a few master-only screens (System Health, Pipeline AI Controls) are noted where they appear.

subs.heading: The persistent chrome (sidebar, breadcrumb, guards)
subs.body:
• Left sidebar — the navy rail, grouped into Overview, Opportunities, Customers, Content, System, and CRM. The brand link RFP Admin returns you to the Dashboard; a Portal → footer link jumps to the customer side.
  • Breadcrumb trail at the top of the content — a click-through history with ‹ Back / › Forward arrows (browser-history semantics, persisted per tab).
  • Unsaved-changes guard — editors (Site pages, AI-config cards) warn “You have unsaved changes on this page. Leave without saving?” if you navigate away dirty.

figures.cap: The admin sidebar — every surface in this guide is one click from here.

table.title: Sidebar map — every destination
rows: Intake · RFP Curation · Opportunity Cards · Sources · Scout Monitor · Pipeline Jobs · Templates · Guardrail Defaults
Applications · Tenants · Billing · Waitlist · Purchases · Proposals
Site Content · Document Builder · S3 Storage
System State · Event Stream · Agents · Automation · Process Monitor · Workflows · Process Ledger · System Health · Analytics

callouts.html: A few surfaces are reachable only by link, not the sidebar: /admin/scouts (from Sources), /admin/intake, /admin/cards, and /admin/opportunities. This guide covers them all.

sections.heading: The Dashboard — your daily starting point
sections.lead: The Dashboard is a system-overview landing: metric tiles up top, your ToDo queue in the middle, and live feeds below. It answers “what needs me right now?”
sections.caption: The admin Dashboard — stat tiles, ToDos, recent events, pending actions.

steps.t: Scan the eight stat tiles. Each tile is a click-through that opens its target page in a new tab. Events Today also shows a hover preview of the six most recent events.
steps.cap: The eight metric tiles — click any to drill in.

steps.t: Work your ToDo queue (“Your To-Dos”). Each card carries an urgency chip (Overdue/Due soon), a workflow-name pill, and a step trail. The action button is typed to the task — see below.
steps.cap: The ToDo queue — typed completers per task.

steps.t: Clear a single ToDo. A review task shows Approve / Done and Dismiss; an acknowledgement shows Acknowledge; an upload task shows Open to upload + Mark uploaded.
steps.cap: A curation ToDo with Approve / Dismiss.

steps.t: Review the feeds. Recent Events (Time · Event · Phase · Actor) and Pending Actions (Pending applications · Unclaimed RFPs · Draft atoms awaiting review) — each row deep-links to the right screen.
steps.cap: Recent Events + Pending Actions.

callouts.html: The ToDo queue (the TaskQueue) auto-reloads every 30s and appears on tenant dashboards too. A Form task renders its own required fields; a Broadcast note just needs an Acknowledge.

subs.heading: The typed ToDo completers
subs.lead: Each ToDo carries the right control for its kind — you never guess how to clear it.

table.title: How each ToDo type is completed

callouts.html: Each card also shows a WorkflowTrail — the step breadcrumb with the current step in bold and finished steps struck through, so you see where the work sits.

sections.heading: Sources — where opportunities come from
sections.lead: Before anything is ingested, you point the platform at where opportunities live. Sources is your bookmarked-sites hub; each source can be opened, scouted, and fed documents. This is setup you do once per site and revisit when a site changes.
sections.caption: The Sources hub — one card per monitored site, with recent changes and activity.

steps.t: Click + New Solicitation (top-right) to jump straight to the RFP upload form, or work an existing card below.

On any card, the five actions are: Open Site (logs a visit, opens the site), Paste Topics (opens the paste-and-parse modal), Upload PDFs (drops files straight into ingest), Add Note (inline admin note), and Scout Now (runs the scraper immediately).
Drag files onto the card’s “Drop PDF files here to upload” zone to ingest without clicking.

callouts.html: Paste Topics opens a modal: paste tab/pipe/comma-separated rows, click Parse Preview to see a table, then Import N Topics. It auto-detects the delimiter.

subs.heading: Source detail — crawl schedule & monitored regions
subs.lead: Click a source name to open its detail page.
subs.caption: Source detail — crawl settings, monitored regions, change history.

steps.t: Toggle Auto-crawl on, then pick a Schedule (Daily 6am UTC, Every 12 hours, Weekly, Every 6 hours, or a Custom cron). Scout Now runs it on demand.
Edit Admin Notes and Visit Instructions inline (Edit → Save).
Add a Monitored Region (Name, Region Type, Content Context, optional selector/sample) so the scout watches a specific part of the page and flags meaningful diffs.
Review Change History — each diff carries a severity pill and a Review button that marks it seen.

sections.heading: Scout Monitor — the worker pool
sections.lead: The scout pool is the fleet of workers that visit your sources on schedule, diff them, and surface new or changed solicitations. This screen is a pure monitor — setup and “Scout Now” live on the Sources page.
sections.caption: Scout Monitor — pool health, recent runs, and detected changes.

steps.t: Read the five metric cards: Active sources · Healthy · Degraded/error · Running scouts · Changes (24h).
Scan the Worker Pool table (Source · Agency · Health · Fails · Last success · Avg run · Last visit). Health is healthy/degraded/error/unknown; a red Fails count needs attention.
Check Recent scout runs and Changes detected to confirm the pool is finding new opportunities.

callouts.html: Scouts run managed and audited — a run that fails on one source continues on the others; nothing dead-ends. Kick a run from Sources → Scout Now.

sections.heading: Intake — stage an opportunity by hand
sections.lead: When you find an opportunity yourself, Intake stages it into the review queue at status new (not yet live) — the manual stand-in for scout discovery.
sections.caption: The Intake form — stage a found opportunity into the triage queue.

steps.t: Fill Title and Agency (both required), plus any of Office · Unit · Solicitation # · Program (SBIR/STTR/BAA/OTA/CSO) · Initial stage (Pre-Release / NOFO) · dates · POC.
Add a Source URL, Description / notes, and internal RFP Expert Notes (carried on the card). Tick Docs were downloadable if applicable.
Click Stage into review queue. On success the form clears and shows Staged ✓ Curate it → linking straight to RFP Curation.

sections.heading: RFP Curation — the ingest → curate → push cockpit
sections.lead: Curation is the heart of the operator’s job. You claim a solicitation, extract its topics, attach compliance, build the volume/section skeleton, and finish with Push — the fan-out that puts the opportunity in every tenant’s pipeline. This is a multi-part workspace; take it in order.
sections.caption: The triage queue — claim, filter, and open solicitations for curation.

steps.t: Use the Filter select to narrow by status (each option shows its count); Refresh re-pulls.
Each row shows Title · Source · Agency · Status · Namespace · Ingested. Click a row to open the workspace.

Per-row actions depend on status: a new row offers Claim; a row you’ve claimed offers Release for AI and Dismiss; an analyzed row offers Open. A stale claim (>24h) shows a stale pill, and a master_admin can Force Release it.
steps.cap: A triage row with its status pill and actions.

subs.heading: Upload an RFP
subs.lead: Bring a solicitation in by hand from + Upload RFP.

steps.t: Fill the Solicitation Metadata (Title + Agency required; Program Office, Program Type, numbers, dates). Filenames auto-fill empty fields.
Drag documents into the Documents zone (PDF/DOCX/XLSX/PPTX/TXT, max 30 MB total). Pick the primary with the radio; others become attachments.

Multi-topic BAA? Drop the individual topic files into the Topic files zone on the same form — each becomes a topic opportunity under this solicitation in one submit (the button shows Upload + N topics). Leave it empty for a single-topic solicitation, or add topic files later from the workspace drop-zone.
Leave ✨ Run Ingest Assist after upload ticked — it parses the docs, auto-builds the compliance matrix, volumes and section molds, and publishes the card(s). Click Upload & Ingest Assist.

callouts.html: A duplicate file is caught (DUPLICATE_FILE) and offers a Go to the existing solicitation → link instead of making a second copy. Malformed PDFs are sanitized on ingest.

subs.heading: The curation workspace
subs.lead: Opening a solicitation gives you the full cockpit. Work top-to-bottom.
subs.caption: The curation workspace — documents, PDF tagging, topics, volumes, compliance matrix.

steps.t: Write the Spotlight-match summary (top). It’s required before Push — an empty summary blocks the fan-out. Save it; the banner turns from rose to green.
Use the quick-nav tabs — Documents · Topics · Compliance · Customer Interest — to jump around.
steps.cap: The workspace quick-nav tabs.

steps.t: Tag compliance variables on the PDF. Select text in the viewer to open Tag as Compliance Variable, pick or add a variable, and save its value — provenance (doc + page) is recorded.

Extract & manage Topics. For a multi-topic BAA, drop the individual topic files into the topic drop-zone — each file becomes its own topic opportunity under this umbrella (text extracted, deduped, linked back to its file). Or Extract Topics (scan the umbrella text), Import all topics from source, Bulk Import, or + Add Topic. Then Manage Compliance to set per-topic overrides (phase-grouped, with presets).
Build Response Volumes. + Add Volume, then per volume + Add required item — each item points at a starter template (mold) and carries its format rules (page limit, font, margins).
Advance the state machine. The action bar shows only the valid next steps: Claim → Release → Start Curation → Request Review → Approve → Push. Push is the fan-out.
steps.cap: The state-machine action bar.

figures.cap: The required Spotlight-match summary + the live DON26BX03-NP002 solicitation.
Source documents + the tagging viewer inside the workspace.

table.title: The compliance matrix — the 18 fields you curate
rows: Page Limit (Technical) · Page Limit (Cost) · Font Family · Font Size · Margins · Line Spacing
Header Required · Header Format · Footer Required · Footer Format
Submission Format · Slides Allowed · Slide Limit · TABA Allowed
PI Must Be Employee · Partner Max % · Clearance Required · ITAR Required

callouts.html: Each matrix field carries a source pill — Verified (green, you confirmed it) or AI (yellow, suggested). Click p.N on a field to jump the PDF viewer to where it was found.

One solicitation + N topic files → N opportunities. Upload the umbrella solicitation, then drop its topic files into the drop-zone — each becomes a topic opportunity under the umbrella (deduped, text-extracted, linked to its file). Push then fans the umbrella + every topic to all tenants, so 20 topic files land 21 cards.

subs.heading: The curation modals
subs.lead: Curation uses a family of modals; here is what each one captures.

table.title: Curation workspace modals
rows: Topic Number · Status · Title · Description · Branch · Tech Focus Areas
Default branch · a topics textarea (auto-detects delimiter, live preview)
drag/drop N topic files · each becomes a topic opportunity (text extracted, deduped, file-linked)
# · Format · Volume Name · Description · Special Requirements · Applies to Phase
# · Type · Name · Required · limits/format · Starter template (mold) · Expert notes
variable name · category · value (with memory suggestions)

callouts.html: Ingest Assist (✨) can build the topics, volumes, items and compliance in one pass — you then refine. It warns before replacing existing structure.

subs.heading: Customer interest & topic detail
subs.body: At the bottom of the workspace, Customer Interest lists tenants who pinned topics under this solicitation — with the topic, pin date, whether they bought a portal, the proposal stage, and a View Portal link (which drops you into that tenant’s workspace). Open a single topic (from the Topics list) to edit its Title, Description, Status, and Tech Focus Areas on the topic detail page.

sections.heading: Opportunity Cards — the fan-out cockpit
sections.lead: After a push, Opportunity Cards is the master view of every opportunity and how it fanned out: curation status, matrix summary, bridge version, and how many tenants it replicated to. It’s the one place with a lifecycle stage control.
sections.caption: Master opportunity cards — curation, matrix, bridge version, replication, and the stage control.

steps.t: Use the filter box to find by title/agency/number/topic. The table auto-refreshes every 30s; the summary reads “N shown · N total · N on bridge · N replicated”.
Sort by any column header (Opportunity · Curation · Matrix · Bridge · Replicated · Stage · Ingested · Close).
Change lifecycle with the “move →” select in the Stage column — it offers only the allowed transitions (nofo → pre_release → open → updated → closed → archived) and records the change.

callouts.html: The related Opportunity Rollup (/admin/opportunities) is a read-only cross-tenant view: per opportunity, how many tenants ranked vs pinned it and each proposal’s build stage.

sections.heading: Purchases — release a bought portal
sections.lead: When a customer buys a proposal portal with a comp code, it lands here as curation_pending with a 72-hour SLA. You release it from the shadow account — releasing provisions the build unlocked and instantiates the compliance matrix and molds from the master solicitation.
sections.caption: The purchases queue — comp-code and Stripe buys, with the release action.

steps.t: Find the curation_pending purchase (watch the 72h clock).
Open the tenant’s build and Release to customer — this provisions the matrix + molds and unlocks the build.
steps.cap: The release control on a pending purchase.

steps.t: Confirm the tenant now sees an unlocked proposal workspace with a populated compliance matrix.

sections.heading: Applications — onboard a founding-cohort company
sections.lead: Founding-cohort applications arrive here. Accepting one provisions a tenant and emails credentials; the row auto-enriches with the applicant’s SBIR award history.
sections.caption: Applications — expand a row to review readiness and accept/reject.

steps.t: Expand a row. It auto-fetches SBIR/STTR Award History (awards, funding, agencies) and shows Contact, Company, Federal Readiness (SAM/CAGE/UEI), Technology, and target programs/agencies.
Write Admin Review Notes (min 10 chars), then Accept or Reject.
On Accept, a green panel returns the new workspace path plus Login Credentials (email + temporary password) and the welcome-email status. Re-accepting never re-creates the tenant or re-sends email.
steps.cap: An application expanded — readiness detail before you decide.

callouts.html: An already-decided application gets a Change Status block (new status + an audit note ≥5 chars). Every status change is audited.

sections.heading: Templates — the section-mold studio
sections.lead: Templates are the section molds a required item points at — the format contract (page limit, margins, font, structure) every provisioned proposal inherits. Author them here, or templify a winning past proposal.
sections.caption: The Template studio — system + custom molds, filterable, previewable.

steps.t: Click + New Template, name it, pick a Type (Technical Volume, Cost Volume, Slide Deck, …) and a Canvas (Letter/DOCX, Slides/PPTX, Spreadsheet), then Create & open editor.
steps.cap: The New Template panel.

steps.t: Filter the library by Type / Agency / Program; Clear filters resets.
steps.cap: A template card with node count + limits.

steps.t: Preview a system template (read-only, with its merge-field chips), or Edit a custom one to open the full canvas editor. Delete removes a custom mold (items fall back to the registry).

callouts.html: System templates carry an indigo System pill and open read-only — use “Save as new” to fork one. Editing saves the canvas back to the mold.

sections.heading: Workflow Monitor — see & control every automation
sections.lead: Every automation runs as a managed workflow — no fire-and-forget. This is the canonical control surface: launch forms, the template catalog with activation, and the live/recent instance monitor with advance, retry, and cancel.
sections.caption: The Workflow Monitor — stats, catalog, active instances, and recent history.

steps.t: Generate Content — Title, Content type, Brief, optional Slug → the CMS pipeline drafts it and parks at a review ToDo within ~10s.
Launch Review Gate — a human-in-the-loop gate: pick Scope, Assign-to role, Due hours, and the entity keys (Opportunity ID is the spine key). It parks a task on the assignee.
steps.cap: The two launch forms — Generate Content + Launch Review Gate.

steps.t: Open Workflow Catalog to see every template with a status dot, description, trigger key, and instance counts (running/paused/done/failed).
Toggle Activate / Deactivate per template. Deactivating refuses new launches (existing instances finish) and is audited.
steps.cap: The catalog with per-template activation.

steps.t: The stats bar shows Running / Paused / Completed 24h / Failed 24h. Active Workflows auto-refreshes every 10s with a live elapsed timer.
steps.cap: A live instance with its progress bar and controls.

steps.t: Click Steps to expand the transition timeline (step · from→to · actor · time · reason).
Advance a paused instance (HITL override), Cancel a running one, or Retry a failed one from Recent History. A failed row’s error toggle shows the failing step + message.
steps.cap: The live stats bar + active instances.

table.title: Workflow instance states
rows: parked on a human gate — Advance to continue

callouts.html: A step that fails continues on independent branches; a human gate parks and resumes. The same runs also appear under the legacy Process Monitor and Process Ledger — treat Workflows as primary.

sections.heading: Automation Rules — event → action
sections.lead: Automation rules fire actions on system events. Each rule watches a namespace:type trigger and runs an action (notify, queue a job, send email, create a ToDo, publish content, …).
sections.caption: Automation rules — triggers, action types, and per-rule toggles.

steps.t: Read the four cards: Total Rules · Active · Inactive · Executions (24h).
In the table, flip a rule’s Active toggle to enable/disable it (optimistic, audited).
steps.cap: An automation rule row with its toggle.

steps.t: View Config expands the action’s JSON; View Logs jumps to the event stream filtered to that trigger.

callouts.html: Action types include queue_notification, send_email, create_todo, distribute_social, publish_content, webhook, and more — each rendered as a colored pill.

sections.heading: Agents — the AI workforce & its budget
sections.lead: The Agents screen is the workforce roster and its usage. Tenant-space agents are tenant-bound and advisory — they propose, a guardrail checks, and a human accepts; they never auto-write business tables.
sections.caption: The agent workforce — roster by pod, per-tenant usage, and cost summary.

steps.t: Read the roster, grouped into four pods (Tenant build & pursue · Master ingestion · Our-org RFP-admin ops · Our-org CMS). Each agent shows scope (🔒 Tenant-bound), what it wakes on, status (live/wired/dormant), 30-day queue, and last run.
steps.cap: The agent roster grouped by pod.

steps.t: Below, Usage by tenant (30 days) and a six-tile Usage Summary (calls, cost, tokens, active tenants).
steps.cap: An agent row with its 30-day queue.

steps.t: A master_admin also gets Pipeline AI Controls — default monthly budget, rate limit, per-call ceiling, and an optional platform-wide monthly cap.
Lower on the page, the Tool Registry (every callable tool, its min role and tenant-scoping) and Recent Tool Invocations give you the full audit of what the agents actually called.
steps.cap: The tool registry + recent invocations — the agent audit trail.

callouts.html: Research Scout (status live): a tenant-bound R&D agent a customer triggers from a proposal’s AI & Library tab (“Research this opportunity”). It browses the web — including DoD sources (SAM.gov, SBIR.gov, DSIP) — through a controlled, SSRF-guarded server-side browser and returns a cited brief. Same safety contract as every agent here: web results injection-fenced (data, never instructions), budget/rate/cost-capped via Pipeline AI Controls, and human-gated (advisory brief, never auto-written). Usage shows in this roster and the tool-invocation audit — the “use more, pay more” model applies.

subs.heading: Guardrail defaults
subs.lead: /admin/guardrail-defaults sets the hard limits every customer portal launches inside.
subs.caption: Guardrail defaults — the safety envelope for new launches.

steps.t: Set Max stages, Max collaborators, Max managers, and Max nudges, then Save limits. Changes apply to future launches; frozen configs are unaffected.

sections.heading: Observability — Events, Process Monitor, Ledger
sections.lead: Three complementary lenses on “what happened, when, and did it finish?” across every tenant.

subs.heading: Event Stream
subs.caption: The event stream — filter by namespace, type, and time window.

steps.t: Filter by Namespace (finder/capture/identity/proposal/library/system/tool), a time window (1h/6h/24h/7d), and toggle Auto-refresh (10s).
Each row shows Time · Event · Phase (start/end/single/error) · Actor · Tenant · Payload (click to expand).
steps.cap: An event row with its phase badge.

steps.t: The filter bar drives everything from the URL, so a filtered view is shareable/bookmarkable.
steps.cap: The event-stream filter bar.

subs.heading: Process Monitor
subs.caption: The process monitor — in-progress, completions, errors, tenant activity.
subs.body: A real-time view built from events: namespace stat cards, an In Progress list (started-without-end), Recent Completions, a collapsible Errors panel (auto-expands when non-zero), and a Tenant Activity (24h) table.

subs.heading: Process Ledger
subs.caption: The process ledger — active instances, health-classified, advanceable inline.
subs.body: The cross-tenant list of active process_instances, health-classified so problems surface first. Filter by health chips (Failing/Stalled/Awaiting/Running) or by tenant, and Advance a paused gate inline.

sections.heading: System State — the operational dashboard
sections.lead: A tabbed operational board that auto-refreshes every 30s. The always-on HealthBar (Active Workflows · Pending Jobs · Events 1h/24h · Automation Rules · Errors 1h) sits above eight tabs.
sections.caption: System State — HealthBar + eight tabs (Overview, Workflows, Pipeline, Content, Email, Trees, Errors, Volume).

steps.t: Start on Overview (top workflows, pipeline, recent errors, event volume).
Drill into Active Workflows (expandable cards with per-step status), Pipeline (sources · curation queue · proposals by stage), Content Pipeline, and Email Automation.
Use Process Trees (recursive event trees), Errors, and Event Volume (stacked hourly chart) to diagnose.

table.title: The eight System-State tabs
rows: top active workflows, pipeline, recent errors, event-volume chart
every running instance as an expandable card with per-step status + JSON
ingestion sources · curation queue by status · proposals by stage
published/draft blocks, pending reviews, content event timeline
rules fired, emails sent/pending, failures, execution log
stacked hourly bar chart by namespace

subs.heading: System Health · Analytics · Storage
subs.body: System Health (/admin/system, master_admin only) is the capacity view — queue depth, tool-invocation latencies (p50/p95), registered tools, recent errors. Analytics (/admin/analytics) rolls up tenants, proposals, atoms, revenue, and visitor traffic. Storage (/admin/storage) is the S3/R2 file manager (Curation Files · Pipeline Artifacts · Customer Storage · Reference Library) with presigned uploads, folders, rename, and bulk actions.

sections.heading: Tenants — oversight & shadow-descend
sections.lead: Tenants is the roster of every company. From a tenant you review its state, tune its AI budget, archive/restore access, and — the operator’s superpower — shadow-descend into its portal to do work on its behalf, then rise back to ingest more.
sections.caption: The tenant roster — users, atoms, proposals per company; + New Company.

steps.t: Create a company with + New Company (name + admin POC email → returns the slug and a temporary password).
Open a tenant to see its users, recent activity, and company details.
steps.cap: A tenant detail page — users, activity, AI budget, archive control.

steps.t: Set an AI Budget & Limits override (monthly budget, rate limit, per-call ceiling) or Archive / Restore access when a license lapses.
steps.cap: The per-tenant AI budget override.

steps.t: Shadow-descend: enter the tenant’s portal (the session rewrites to tenant_admin, a shadow banner shows), do the work, and return to /admin. Everything stays audited to their trail.
steps.cap: Shadow-descend — working inside a tenant’s portal, banner shown.

callouts.html: One account, both jobs. eric@rfppipeline.com ingests at /admin, descends into Immobileyes to build, then rises back up — no separate login.

sections.heading: Billing & Waitlist

figures.cap: Billing — revenue, recent purchases, subscription status.

sections.body: Billing summarizes revenue, recent purchases (with status pills), and per-tenant subscription status. Waitlist is a read-only list of marketing-page email captures with a View Applications link.

sections.heading: Site Content — the dynamic-content editor
sections.lead: The public marketing site is edited here as versioned blocks: every save is a snapshot, and publishing swaps the live version the public site reads. This is the same “dynamic content section” model these very manuals use — edit data, publish, done.
sections.caption: Site Content — pages, site chrome, and documents, each version-controlled.

steps.t: Pick a Page (or the Header & Footer, or a Document). Each row shows its live version and draft state.
steps.cap: A site page row with its version + state.

steps.t: Edit the blocks — section name, Title, Body, Excerpt, image (with upload), icon, and metadata JSON. + Add block appends one.
Add an audit note, then Preview (iframe of the public path), Save draft, or Publish (makes it live).

subs.heading: Document Builder
subs.body: Document Builder (/admin/documents) authors standalone canvas documents (templates, examples, reference). New Document picks a format preset; the editor is the full canvas with save, multi-format Export (docx/pptx/xlsx), and version History (restore any prior save).
